comment: Scripted mock session replayed by MockAudioSource/MockTranscriber. `at` is the session clock in seconds (drives timestamps); `delay` is playback ms since the previous event (compressed vs the clock so the whole demo runs in ~2 minutes). Covers: confident match, points striking through, ambiguous question with the 4s auto-pick, a question absent from the bank, a long answer, a ⌘K override, collapse/expand, and session end.

events.text: Thanks for making the time. So to start — tell me about a time you handled
So to start — tell me about a time you handled a really difficult employee relations case.
Sure — the riskiest one was two complainants against one long-tenured supervisor, at a site that was used to silence.
First move was to separate the people, not the payroll — schedule changes, no suspensions.
I ran eleven interviews in five days and documented as I went,
and in the end the supervisor left the business.
say a harassment complaint lands on your desk
Say a harassment complaint lands on your desk — how do you run the investigation?
I'm careful about interview order — complainant first, then witnesses, the respondent last.
And I make the credibility calls on the record, not in my head.
What's your approach to pay transparency conversations, when someone finds out a peer earns more?
Honestly, I start from the range architecture — if the bands are defensible, the conversation is about the band, not the person.
Something closer to home — I've got a manager who's burning their team out.
I've got a manager who's burning their team out — how do you coach a manager in that spot?
I'd show them their own attrition and overtime numbers first — those tell the story better than I can.
Then coach the behaviour, not the intention — almost none of them mean to do it.
And set a review date, because coaching without a checkpoint is a hope, not a plan.
We're about to roll out a return-to-office policy nobody is going to love — walk me through how you'd land it.
First, name the cost honestly on day one — people smell spin.
And publish the exception path, because pressure needs a valve.
Before we wrap — what would you want to know from us before accepting an offer?
Two things — how the team defines a good first ninety days, and what burned out the last person in this seat.
